questions.q: What is Psychology?
options: A study of cognitive processes & behavior
questions.explanation: Week 0 is a general pre-course quiz with no lectures; answer is standard introductory psychology. Psychology = scientific study of mind (cognitive processes) and behavior.

questions.q: A broad field of study that explores a variety of questions about thoughts, feelings and actions is___?
questions.explanation: Week 0 is a general pre-course quiz with no lectures; answer is standard introductory psychology.

questions.q: A systematic assessment that provides information on political views, consumer buying habits and many other topics is called___?
questions.explanation: Week 0 is a general pre-course quiz with no lectures; answer is standard introductory psychology. Surveys gather data on political views, buying habits etc.

questions.q: The word Psyche means
questions.explanation: Week 0 is a general pre-course quiz with no lectures; answer is standard introductory psychology. Greek psyche = mind/soul.

questions.q: Who established psychology laboratory in Germany?
questions.explanation: Week 0 is a general pre-course quiz with no lectures; answer is standard introductory psychology. Wundt founded the first lab at Leipzig (1879).

questions.q: To help people to function effectively and fulfill their own unique potential" is the aim of___?
questions.explanation: Week 0 is a general pre-course quiz with no lectures; answer is standard introductory psychology. Humanistic psychology aims at self-actualization.

questions.q: Behaviorists use a learning process to change abnormal behavior is called___?
questions.explanation: Week 0 is a general pre-course quiz with no lectures; answer is standard introductory psychology. Behaviour therapy uses conditioning.

questions.q: The study of changes in behavior during life time is called
questions.explanation: Week 0 is a general pre-course quiz with no lectures; answer is standard introductory psychology.

questions.q: The study of differences and similarities in the behavior of animals of different species is called
questions.explanation: Week 0 is a general pre-course quiz with no lectures; answer is standard introductory psychology.

questions.q: Which of the following is true regarding learning in psychology?
options: Learning has not been an important topic in psychology
Learning involves no change in the organism
Learning focuses on how humans speak
Learning can be defined in many ways
questions.explanation: Lecture: learning "has been defined differently by different group of psychologists"; the other options contradict the lecture. (Lecture 1: Psychology of Learning)

questions.q: Learning is seen as an effect attributed to an element in
questions.explanation: "observable change in the behavior that is attributed to an element in the environment" (Lecture 1: Psychology of Learning)

questions.q: Non-associative learning refers to ____________ in the intensity of a response as the result of the repeated presentation of a stimulus.
questions.explanation: "the non-associative learning ... refers to the decrease in the intensity of a response" (Lecture 1: Psychology of Learning)

questions.q: Which of the following is a type of learning style?
questions.explanation: "visual learners, auditory learners, kinesthetic learners" are named as learner preferences. (Lecture 2: Psychology of Learning (Contd.))

questions.q: 'Psychology as the Behaviorist Views It' is the famous work of
questions.explanation: "his work is the psychology as the behaviorist views it" (Watson). (Lecture 2: Psychology of Learning (Contd.))

questions.q: The state of conscious incompetence may be valuable ____________ of a learning experience.
questions.explanation: "the state of conscious incompetent may be valuable at the start of learning" (Lecture 2: Psychology of Learning (Contd.))

questions.q: Adding to existing student knowledge is known as
questions.explanation: "adding to the existing student knowledge known as the conceptual growth" (Lecture 3)

questions.q: Deliberate practice involves the following, except
questions.explanation: "deliberate practice involves attention rehearsal and repetition over time" (Lecture 4)

questions.q: Students persist in the face of challenging tasks and process information more deeply when they adopt ____________ goals.
questions.explanation: Principle: students persist ... and process information more deeply when they adopt mastery goals (APA principle, read in lecture). (Lecture 4)

questions.q: ____________ refers to a decrease in response rate while ____________ refers to an increase in response rate.
questions.explanation: Habituation = reduced response through regular exposure; sensitization described as "just opposite" (heightened response). (Lecture 5)

questions.q: According to constructivism, reality is determined by
options: the blood type of the learner
the future goals of the learner
questions.explanation: Constructivism: learners construct knowledge from their own experiences. (Lecture 10)

questions.q: Teachers and instructors who understand the constructivist learning theory understand that their students
options: do not demand much effort in the classroom
questions.explanation: "students bring their own unique experience in their classroom". (Lecture 10)

questions.q: The domain of social constructivism is largely attributed to the work done by ____________ by adding the focus on societal and peer influence on learning.
questions.explanation: "social constructivism ... Lev Vygotsky ... societies and peer influence has a significant role". (Lecture 10)

questions.q: Which of the following is not a major type of learning described by behavioral psychology?
questions.explanation: Behavioural psychology's three types: classical, operant, observational learning; "traditional learning" is not one. (Lecture 2: Psychology of Learning (Contd.))

questions.q: Which of the following is true according to behaviorism?
options: all behaviors are directed by one's parents
all behaviors are fundamentally destructive in nature
questions.explanation: "behavior can be unlearned can be unlearned and replaced by the new behavior" (Lecture 6: Major Theories of Learning)

questions.q: In ____________ conditioning, presentation of unconditioned stimulus precedes the presentation of the conditioned stimulus.
questions.explanation: "backward condition is that an unconditioned stimulus precedes the presentation of the [conditioned] stimulus" (Lecture 6: Major Theories of Learning)

questions.q: Smiling and complimenting students for good performance is a type of
questions.explanation: Praise/smiles added after good performance = positive reinforcement (operant conditioning, lecture 6).

questions.q: Which of the following psychologists was instrumental in engendering the dramatic shift from behaviorism to cognitive theories?
questions.explanation: "Tolman ... Bruner ... German Gestalt psychologists ... instrumental in changing ... bringing this cognitive theories". (Lecture 7)

questions.q: IQ is a typical measurement for
questions.explanation: IQ is the standard measure of intelligence (lecture 8 intelligence theories). (Lecture 8)

questions.q: BBL deals with the concept of learning in a ____________ context.
questions.explanation: "brain based learning ... the concept of learning in a neurophysiological context". (Lecture 9)

questions.q: Which of the following is true?
options: Human memory involves the ability to only preserve information
Human memory involves the ability to only recover information
Human memory involves the ability to neither preserve nor recover information
Human memory involves the ability to both preserve and recover information
questions.explanation: Memory = encoding, storage and retrieval, i.e. both preserving and recovering information. (Lecture 11: Memory & Cognition)

questions.q: ____ refers to connections between the nerve cells
questions.explanation: "changes in this connection between the nerve cells ... synapses". (Lecture 11: Memory & Cognition)

questions.q: In order to create a new memory, information must be changed into ____
questions.explanation: "information must be changed to a usable form". (Lecture 11: Memory & Cognition)

questions.q: The memory ____ process allows us to bring stored memories into conscious awareness.
questions.explanation: "memory retrieval process also allows us to bring the stored memory into the conscious awareness". (Lecture 11: Memory & Cognition)

questions.q: Which of the following is not a major domain of cognition?
questions.explanation: Domains of cognition: attention, perception, memory, intelligence, executive function, social cognition, judgment; not aggression. (Lecture 11: Memory & Cognition)

questions.q: Which of the following is not an assumption of the information processing view?
options: Information is processed in steps or stages
There are limits on how much information can be processed
The human information processing system is interactive
Information processing is analogous to computer processing
questions.explanation: The question looks flawed: Lecture 11 lists all four options as assumptions of information processing (the 2024 version says "There is no limit"). The answer key gives this option.

questions.q: ____ refers to rote rehearsal of repetition
questions.explanation: Maintenance rehearsal = rote repetition.

questions.q: ____ presentations can enhance working memory capacity
questions.explanation: Not found in the captions; dual-channel working memory (lecture 13) implies multimodal (audio+visual) presentation increases effective capacity.

questions.q: Episodic and semantic memories are categorized under ____ memory
questions.explanation: Episodic and semantic memory are subtypes of declarative (explicit) memory. (Lecture 14)

questions.q: According to the neural network model, memory capacity depends on ____
options: spatial and temporal correlations between memories
questions.explanation: "memory capacity ... depends on the complexity of the synapses, the sparseness of the representation, the spatial and temporal [correlations]". (Lecture 14)

questions.q: Creative thinking is the ability to generate ____ ideas.
questions.explanation: Creative thinking generates new, unconventional and useful ideas (lecture 19); all of the above.

questions.q: ____ are representative items within each concept.
questions.explanation: Prototypes are representative items of a concept. (Lecture 16: Thinking & Cognition)

questions.q: A mental representation can take the form of a ____.
questions.explanation: Mental representations take the form of images, musical tones, words, etc. (Lecture 16: Thinking & Cognition)

questions.q: Which of the following is true?
options: Thinking is a lower mental process
Thinking is unrelated to problem solving
We can only think in numbers or words
questions.explanation: "thinking is a sub vocal talking"; thinking is a higher-level function. (Lecture 16: Thinking & Cognition)

questions.q: Cognitive architecture is a theory about the ____ that create a mind in natural or artificial systems.
questions.explanation: "cognitive architecture is the structure"; a theory of the fixed structures that make up a mind. (Lecture 14)

questions.q: Bloom's Taxonomy is a system of hierarchical models (arranged in a hierarchical rank,) used to categorize ____ into varying levels of complexity.
questions.explanation: Bloom's taxonomy classifies learning (educational) objectives by complexity. (Lecture 17)

questions.q: ____ knowledge refers to knowledge of terminology and specific details.
questions.explanation: "factual knowledge ... relates to specific details, information, data" (terminology and details). (Lecture 17)

questions.q: Choosing to skim subheadings of unimportant information to get to the information we need as a metacognitive skill is called ____.
questions.explanation: Metacognitive skill examples: knowing limits, self-monitoring, modifying, "skimming". (Lecture 18)

questions.q: ____ refers to the ability to regulate your thoughts and set aside any personal biases to come to the best conclusion.
questions.explanation: Corrected after checking the lecture (was: Openmindedness). Lecture: "self regulation ... whenever we are reaching ... the conclusion ... we have to keep aside our personal bias ... regulating ... monitoring our thought processes" = self-regulation, not open-mindedness. (Lecture 18)

questions.q: ____ method of solving problems refers to a rule that guarantees the solution to a problem
questions.explanation: Algorithm = rule/procedure that guarantees a solution (vs heuristics/trial and error).

questions.q: Motivation is seen as a ____ that drives and directs human behavior.
questions.explanation: L21 slide: 'Motivation is seen as a mental impulse that drives and directs human behavior'.

questions.q: Which of the following is false regarding motivation?
questions.explanation: L21 slide: motivation is 'an internal process that can't be directly observed', so 'can be directly observed' is false.

questions.q: Which of the following does not come under intrinsic motivation?
questions.explanation: L21: intrinsic factors are needs, interest, curiosity, self-satisfaction; social pressure is an extrinsic causal factor.

questions.q: Doing something/behaving well because one feels pressure from within is called ____.
questions.explanation: L21: introjected regulation = 'doing something or behave well because one feels pressure within'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a biological need/drive?
questions.explanation: L22 slide: biological drives relate to food, water, shelter, sex; love is a psychological drive.

questions.q: ____ theory suggests that people are motivated to take action in order to receive a reward
questions.explanation: L22 slide: incentive theory 'suggests that people are motivated to take action in order to receive a reward'.

questions.q: The Arousal Theory of Motivation was first proposed by ____.
questions.explanation: L22 slide: 'The Arousal Theory of Motivation was first proposed by Henry Murray in 1938'.

questions.q: ____ theory is based on the assumption that our behavior is based on making a conscious choice from a set of possible alternative behaviors.
questions.explanation: L22 slide: expectancy theory 'is based on the assumption that our behavior is based on making a conscious choice from a set of possible alternative behaviors'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not an attribute of effective goal setting?
questions.explanation: L23: effective goals are specific, measurable, assignable, realistic, time-based; unrealistic goals are not an attribute.

questions.q: Maslow's hierarchy of needs consists of ____ tiers.
questions.explanation: L24: Maslow's 'five tier model... five layers'.

questions.q: ____ is mainly responsible for popularizing emotional intelligence.
questions.explanation: L26 slide: 'Dr. Daniel Goleman popularized the term in his 1995 book'.

questions.q: EQ is used to measure ____.
questions.explanation: L26: emotional intelligence and emotional quotient (EQ) are used interchangeably; EQ measures EI.

questions.q: Experts suggest that EQ is more important than IQ.
questions.explanation: L26: 'expert says that EQ is more important than the IQ'.

questions.q: Being able to put words to feelings refers to ____.
questions.explanation: L26: putting feelings into words 'is called the emotional literacy'.

questions.q: The first step in emotional intelligence is ____.
questions.explanation: L27: 'perceiving emotions in the beginning first step... first is perceiving emotion'.

questions.q: According to nine-layer model pyramid, ____ lies at the bottom of the pyramid.
questions.explanation: L27: the nine-layer pyramid starts 'with emotional stimuli' at its base.

questions.q: The mixed model by ____ claims that EQ is a combination of competencies, skills, and “facilitators” that contribute to how people express themselves, respond to challenges in their environment, and connect with others.
questions.explanation: L27: 'Bar-On's mixed model... says that EQ is a combination of competencies, skills and facilitators'.

questions.q: The transfer of emotions from one person to another is called ____.
questions.explanation: L29 slide: 'emotional contagion - the transfer of emotional state from person to person'.

questions.q: Hochschild has given the concept of ____ using the example of flight attendants.
questions.explanation: L29: emotional labor illustrated with flight attendants (Hochschild).

questions.q: Review of literature shows that ____ is associated with increasing levels of burnout.
questions.explanation: L29: 'surface acting is associated with increasing level of burnout' (teacher burnout literature).

questions.q: Which of the following is false about learning according to Gagne’s definition?
options: It is a change in human disposition
It persists over a period of time
It is simply ascribable to processes of growth
questions.explanation: L31: Gagne - learning 'is not simply ascribable to processes of growth'.

questions.q: Manual or physical skills come under ____ component of Bloom’s taxonomy.
questions.explanation: L31: psychomotor domain covers reflex/fundamental movements, physical activities, skilled movement.

questions.q: Reflection, learning and education was explored by ____.
questions.explanation: L31 slide: 'John Dewey's Reflection, learning and education: Returning to experience...'.

questions.q: The principles of ____ refer to how close in time two events must be for a bond to be formed.
questions.explanation: L31: principle of contiguity - how close in time two events must be for a bond to form (behaviorist orientation).

questions.q: ____ gives information to learners about their success or failure concerning the task at hand.
questions.explanation: L31: 'cognitive feedback... gives the idea to the learner how successful he has been, where is the failure' (knowledge of results).

questions.q: The ____ orientation to learning has a quality of personal involvement—the whole person in both feeling and cognitive aspects being in the learning event.
questions.explanation: L31: humanistic orientation (Carl Rogers) - 'not just about only cognition but cognition and feeling', personal involvement.

questions.q: Learning through play is ____ learning.
questions.explanation: L32: active learning = learning by doing, 'learning by playing', experimenting.

questions.q: People with ____ learning style are prone to sorting their ideas after speaking, rather than thinking ideas through before.
questions.explanation: L32: auditory learners learn by 'speaking... reading aloud, sorting their ideas after speaking'.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is false?
questions.explanation: L33: effective instruction 'is generative and dynamic, it's not fixed', eclectic, interactive - so 'static' is false.

questions.q: In ADDIE model, I stand for ____.
questions.explanation: L33: ADDIE - analysis, design, development, implementation, evaluation.

questions.q: Pedagogy can be defined as a way of ____ any theoretical topic or academic subject.
questions.explanation: L36: pedagogy 'can be defined as a way of teaching of both the theoretical subjects, practical subjects'.

questions.q: Good pedagogy is about ____.
options: enabling self to be good at rote memorization
questions.explanation: L36: 'the primary focus of good pedagogy... is to elicit the responses that demonstrate that understanding'.

questions.q: Which of the following is a pedagogical approach in teaching?
questions.explanation: L36 slide: integrative approach is one of the five pedagogical approaches.

questions.q: According to the ____ approach, learners are the makers of meaning and knowledge.
questions.explanation: L36: in the constructivist approach 'Learners are the makers of the meaning and knowledge'.

questions.q: Which of the following is false about inquiry-based learning?
options: is a form of passive learning
generally used in small scale investigations
questions.explanation: L36: inquiry-based 'is a form of active learning', starts by posing questions, problem-based, 'used in the small scale investigation' - so 'passive' is false.

questions.q: The ____ model describes what effective teachers do in their classrooms to engage students in intellectually challenging work.
questions.explanation: L36: 'the pedagogical model... what effective teachers do in the classroom to engage the students in intellectually challenging work'.

questions.q: In experiential learning, experiences are structured to require the student to ____.
questions.explanation: L37 slide: 'Experiences are structured to require the student to take initiative, make decisions and be accountable for results'.

questions.q: The following are the roles of an instructor in experiential learning, except ____.
questions.explanation: L37 slide: roles are 'setting suitable experiences, posing problems, setting boundaries, supporting students...'; blurring boundaries is not a role.

questions.q: Kolb's experiential learning style theory is typically represented by a ____-stage learning cycle
questions.explanation: L37: Kolb's 'four stage learning cycle'.

questions.q: People with ____ learning style are hands-on learners, and rely on intuition over logic.
questions.explanation: L37: 'accommodating is more of hands-on learners, they rely more on intuition, gut feeling, relying on others'.

questions.q: A ____ classroom is the changing face of learning.
questions.explanation: L41: the digital classroom 'has completely changed the face of learning and education in 21st century'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a feature of e-learning?
questions.explanation: Lecture 41 slide lists the features of e-learning: "Accessibility, user friendliness and social justice; Personalization, individualization and learner-centeredness". It is learner-centred, not teacher-centred.

questions.q: Which of the following is a synonym of e-learning?
questions.explanation: L41 slide: 'It is not a synonym of audio-visual learning, multimedia learning, distance learning as these are just complementary.'

questions.q: In ____ e-learning course, the content is simple and comprises text, images, audio, powerpoint presentation and text questions.
questions.explanation: L41 slide: 'Text Driven: In a text-driven e-learning course, the content is simple and comprises text, images, audio, power-point presentation and text questions.'

questions.q: Recent thinking in cognitive psychology places the ____ firmly at the center of the learning experience.
questions.explanation: L42: 'recent thinking on the cognitive psychology places the individual firmly at the center'.

questions.q: Which of the following is true?
questions.explanation: L42: principles - learning is goal oriented, learning depends on self-awareness, learning is social (and active).

questions.q: Learners may multitask when engaging in an online course, which could be resulting in ____.
questions.explanation: L43: continuous multitasking 'makes our attention span very short'.

questions.q: The brain can process ____ visual cues per hour!
questions.explanation: L42 slide: 'The brain can process 36,000 visual cues per hour!'

questions.q: Our brain has approximately ____ neurons that send information to one another.
questions.explanation: L42 slide: 'Our brain has approximately 85 billion neurons that send information to one another.'

questions.q: ____ is referring to learners' automatic performance on specific procedures with predetermined steps to be followed.
questions.explanation: L44 slide: 'Chaining is referring to learners' automatic performance on specific procedures...' - keyed term is chaining.

questions.q: The ____ Model for New Normal in Education has been designed by many educational institutions.
questions.explanation: L46: 'Readiness model for the New Normal education has been prepared'.

questions.q: The most critical factor that plays a significant role in the success of any remote learning program is the ____.
questions.explanation: L46 slide: 'Learners' Readiness: The most critical factor that plays a significant role in the success of any remote learning program is the readiness of the participants.'

questions.q: The typical picture of a teacher being a ____ of knowledge to the students has been replaced.
questions.explanation: L46 slide: 'the typical picture of a teacher being a dispenser of knowledge to the students has been replaced by that of a facilitator'.

questions.q: What does today's teacher need to be successful in the classroom?
questions.explanation: L46: today's teacher needs digital skills, life skills, communication skills (plus creativity etc.).

questions.q: Students who consider intelligence as a ____ entity tend to focus on their goals despite obstacles.
questions.explanation: L46 slide (Principle 1): 'Students who consider intelligence as a malleable entity tend to focus on their goals despite obstacles.'

questions.q: ____ feedback to students is important for learning.
questions.explanation: L47 principle 6: 'clear, explanatory and timely feedback to students is very important for learning'.

questions.q: Students tend to enjoy learning and have better outcomes when their motivation is more intrinsic than extrinsic.
questions.explanation: L47 principle 9: motivation more intrinsic than extrinsic gives more enjoyment and better outcomes.

questions.q: Long term goals are also called ____ goals.
questions.explanation: L47 slide (Principle 12): 'Short-term (proximal), specific and challenging objectives are more motivating than long-term (distal), general' ones.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a reward?
questions.explanation: L48 slide: 'A reward may be social, such as clapping, or tangible, such as giving' money; verbal praise/compliments also rewards - all of the above.

questions.q: ____ is a teaching approach that generates feedback students can use to improve their performance.
questions.explanation: L49: 'assessment for learning is also a teaching approach that generates the feedback to the students that can use to improve their performance'.

questions.q: Social cognition is the cognitive processes that influence ____.
questions.explanation: L51: 'social cognition is the cognitive process that influences social behavior'.

questions.q: Smooth and adaptive social interactions depend on the recruitment of ____.
questions.explanation: L51 slide: 'Smooth and adaptive social interactions depend on the recruitment of virtually all core cognitive functions (e.g., perception, attention, language, memory, executive functions)'.

questions.q: Which of the following abilities does not come under social cognition?
questions.explanation: L51 slide: social cognition includes face processing, joint attention, theory of mind, moral reasoning, social decision-making; rote memory is not listed.

questions.q: Social cognition develops primarily in old age.
questions.explanation: L51: 'social cognition develops in childhood and adolescence' - not primarily in old age.

questions.q: A theory of mind refers to a person’s ability to understand and think about the ____ of other people.
questions.explanation: L52: 'theory of mind refers to the person's ability to understand and think about the mental state of others'.

questions.q: The ____ theory details the processes of observational learning and modeling, and the influence of self-efficacy on the production of behavior.
questions.explanation: L52: social cognitive theory deals with 'observational learning, modeling and the influence of self-efficacy'.

questions.q: ____ processes account for the information that is selected for observation in the environment.
questions.explanation: L53: 'attentional processes ... account for the information that is selected for observation'.

questions.q: Children become more aggressive when they observe aggressive or violent models.
questions.explanation: L53: 'children become more aggressive when they observe the aggressive or violent models'.

questions.q: The ____ model of observational learning involves real or fictional characters displaying behaviors in books, films, television programs, or online media.
questions.explanation: L53: symbolic model - characters from fiction, books, films, television or online media.

questions.q: ____ refers to the anticipated consequences of a person’s behavior.
questions.explanation: L54: 'expectation is the anticipated consequence of the person's behavior'.

questions.q: Sustainability in the context of environmental sustainability is ____.
questions.explanation: L56 slide (Eggert 2009): 'Sustainability as used in environmental sustainability, economic sustainability and social sustainability is a one dimensional concept'.

questions.q: As discussed by the Brundtland commission, sustainable development was the solution to the problems of ____.
questions.explanation: L56: 'sustainable development was the solution to the problems of environmental degradation discussed by the Brundtland commission'.

questions.q: Environmental sustainability focuses on the impacts of processes, products and services on ____.
questions.explanation: L56: impacts of processes, products and services on air, water, land, biodiversity, human health, ocean environment.

questions.q: Social entrepreneurship is defined as solving social problems using ____.
questions.explanation: L56 slide: 'Social entrepreneurship, defined as solving social problems using market-based methods'.

questions.q: HESI stands for.
questions.explanation: L57: 'higher education sustainability initiative' (HESI).

questions.q: Universal primary and secondary education is an outcome target of ____.
questions.explanation: L57: SDG 4 target 4.1 - universal primary and secondary education.

questions.q: ____ is a target group for ESD for 2030 framework.
questions.explanation: L57: ESD for 2030 target groups - policy makers, institutional leaders, teachers, learners, parents, educators, youth, community.

questions.q: Successful implementation of ESD requires a shift in focus to ____.
questions.explanation: L58 slide: 'Successful implementation of ESD requires a shift in focus from teaching to learning'.

questions.q: ____ competency refers to the ability to reflect on one's own role in community and society.
questions.explanation: L58/L59: 'self-awareness competencies - our ability to reflect on our own role in the local community as well as the global society'.

questions.q: In 2021, the European Centre for the Development of Vocational Training published a skills forecast scenario on the likely employment and skills implications of the ____.
questions.explanation: L60 slide: 'In 2021, the European Centre for the Development of Vocational Training published a skills forecast scenario on the likely employment and skills implications of the European Green Deal'.

questions.q: Which of the following is true regarding learning in psychology?
options: The psychology of learning focuses on how people learn and how they interact with the environments in which they have not learnt
Learning does not involve any changes in the organism
Learning is a relatively temporary change in behavior
questions.explanation: Lecture: learning is a relatively permanent change; options a-c are all false, so "none of the given". (Lecture 1: Psychology of Learning)

questions.q: In order to say that learning has occurred, a/an ___ must occur during the lifetime of the organism.
questions.explanation: "it is an observable change in the behavior that is attributed to an element in the environment" (Lecture 1: Psychology of Learning)

questions.q: Learning changes the ___ through the process of continuous interactions between the learner and the external environment.
options: chemical structure of the spinal cord
questions.explanation: "learning changes the physical structure of the brain through the process of continuous interaction between the learner and the external environment" (Lecture 1: Psychology of Learning)

questions.q: Watson, one of the first psychologists to study learning and behavior is known for the

questions.q: Which of the following is not explored and described by the psychology of learning?
